segments.start_exact: Keesh lived long ago on the rim of the polar sea, was head man
segments.end_exact: came to live in the meanest of all the igloos.
segments.summary: Framing introduction to the legend of Keesh, his heritage, his brave father's death, and his fall into poverty.
segments.reason: Expository framing/backstory establishing the legend; no on-stage GACD or ERAC. Time is generalized and functions as narrative prologue.

segments.start_exact:
It was at a council, one night, in the big igloo of
Klosh-Kwan, the chief, that Keesh showed the blood
segments.end_exact:
but his jaw was set and he went his way, looking
neither to right nor left.
segments.summary: At the council Keesh demands fair meat, is mocked and threatened by the men, and vows to hunt his own meat and enforce fairness before storming out.

gacd.goal: To win recognition and fair distribution of meat for himself and his mother
gacd.action: Keesh rises and confronts the assembled hunters with his grievance and his father's legacy
gacd.conflict: The men are outraged, jeer, threaten beatings and deny him meat

segments.reason: Clear GACD: Keesh's goal (fair meat/recognition), his on-stage confrontation, strong conflict with the hostile council, and a disastrous outcome (jeered out). Unified time/place at the night council.

segments.start_exact:
The next day he went forth along the shore-line where the ice
and the land met together.
segments.end_exact: after that slept for twenty running hours.
segments.summary: Keesh sets out to hunt alone; after a storm and fears of his death, he returns triumphantly bearing bear meat and instructs the men to fetch the rest.
segments.reason: Spans several days summarizing his departure and triumphant return; the actual hunt happens off-stage, so no on-stage GACD conflict. Narrative summary unified by the hunting-return episode.

segments.start_exact:
There was much doubt at first, much doubt and
discussion.
segments.end_exact: the news of the killing might be told. f”
segments.summary: Keesh's repeated hunting success deepens the mystery and rumors of witchcraft; he builds a large igloo, and spies Bim and Bawn follow him and report his strange method to the council.
segments.reason: Extended summary of ongoing success, growing rumors, and the spies' report; time is generalized over many trips without a single on-stage GACD conflict/outcome. Narrative unity around the mystery.

segments.start_exact: And in the afternoon of that day the women hauled in the meat
segments.end_exact:
neither widow nor weak one
cried aloud in the night because there was no meat.
segments.summary: The council confronts Keesh at his igloo demanding explanation; challenged about witchcraft, he reveals his clever whalebone-and-blubber method, resolving the mystery, and rises to head man.

gacd.goal: Keesh must answer the accusation of witchcraft and defend his standing
gacd.action: He receives the council and demonstrates his whalebone trick to prove headcraft not witchcraft
gacd.conflict: The council sternly demands explanation, suspecting witchcraft

segments.reason: GACD present: goal to answer accusation, on-stage demonstration meeting the council's suspicion (conflict), resolved successfully. Unified by time/place at his igloo; closing lines are the tale's resolution kept with the scene.
